namedGrammarLimits.grammarLimit: valid bash: [[ "$char" =~ [[:space:],:] ]] — regex match against a POSIX character class; the vendored grammar recovers with a missing node
valid bash: value=${value/]/%5D} — parameter expansion whose pattern is a literal ] ; the vendored grammar recovers with a missing node

policy: Every tracked .sh/.bash file in clean fsharp@22a8a5dc is audited through the production parseFile pipeline. The analyzer never crashes and never synthesizes phantom rows. Two real files contain valid bash edge constructs (a POSIX-class regex match inside [[ ]] and a ] pattern in a parameter expansion) that the vendored tree-sitter-bash grammar does not model; they are recorded as named grammar limitations by bash-corpus-errors.ts, never hidden. Clean acceptance files are those with zero parse errors.
